Living itself can be a reason to live. Giving meaning to the meaningless can, itself, be your reason for being. Normally, one wouldn't have to come to such an epiphany to keep living and to thrive. Unfortunately, since most of our deep social structures and supports have been damaged or taken from us (religion, family, community, etcetera), we think we have to go through the arduous task of justifying our own existence, but perhaps the existence itself can serve as its own justification.

If you take everything to its logical conclusion in terms of whether or not it has inherent value or meaning, you will find that you ultimately have two ways to look at everything in life: the nihilistic way, from which it follows that nothing has inherent meaning, and therefore nothing has meaning, nothing has reason, and I may as well die; or the vital way, from which it follows that nothing has inherent meaning, and so we can therefore create our own meaning and purpose, we can assign our own value to different actions and beliefs and entities, we can invest in them by spending moments of our life on them, and we can take that artificial meaning and make something worthwhile out of it, which may in time come to organically generate meaning on its own. Because if we can give something meaning, intentionally and out of our own free will, then isn't that in and of itself beautiful and deep? Doesn't that have great significance? Doesn't it make you want to live on, thrive, and continue to find ways to give meaning to the things and the people and the places around you?

From there, I realize that I don't want to die. I think that wanting to die is the single ugliest desire borne by the human heart. I don't think you have to necessarily want to live and overflow with vivid joy to be living with meaning. But I think a good place to start is realizing that you don't want to die. "I don't want to die" explains everything, and is perfectly in line with our natural and biological directive. I don't want to die, and so I won't kill myself. Should I clean my room today? Should I work hard? Well, do I want to die? I don't want to die, so I'll clean my room. I don't want to die, so I'll work hard. I'll take care of myself. I'll help those close to me, and if I have no one then I'll find someone close to me. I don't want to die, so I'll have children. I'll be a good father, so that they will never have to think so hard about whether they want to die or not. And maybe, if we all do this, we can slowly start to build something of meaning in this soulless contemporary age.

It isn't about just surviving. Survival isn't life. Survival is desperate, whereas living is natural. But the first step to living is surviving. And once you can comfortably survive, maybe you'll find that you can slowly come to comfortably live, too.

It might seem like nonsense, or like it's just a trick of the tongue and mind to convince someone that they can find meaning.
